class.name: PhysXSeaCaveWater3D
class.brief_description: Draws the sea inside sea caves, with the waves that reflect off the walls.
class.description: [code]CaveNetwork3D[/code] carries the sea into each sea cave as a long wave along the passage (its surge, which answers the water contract there). This node draws that water: one surface per sea cave along the passage's line, from the arch in, each row at the water's level and half width with its current, from [code]CaveNetwork3D.get_sea_cave_water()[/code], rebuilt every frame. The surface is [PhysXRiver3D]'s (clear water, sky and sun reflections, white water, and the path tracer's refracting medium). The ocean ([PhysXWaterSurface3D]) cuts its own surface out along the passage ([code]CaveNetwork3D.get_water_clip_capsules()[/code]); the two cross-fade over [member fade_length] in from the arch. On the surface run the short waves that come in at the mouth, as Water Surface Wavelets (Jeschke et al. 2018): an amplitude per place and direction, carried at the waves' group speed and by the current, mirrored off the walls and the back of the cave (keeping [member wall_reflection] of their height), fading over [member wave_decay_time], and drawn as real geometry with a shared wave profile (waves 0.6 to 4 m long). Steep faces where they pile up break white. A [code]CaveNetwork3D[/code] with sea caves makes one of these for itself while [code]sea_surge[/code] is on.

link.title: Water Surface Wavelets (Jeschke, Skrivan, Mueller-Fischer, Chentanez, Macklin, Wojtan 2018)

method.name: get_ribbon_count
method.description: The number of sea caves drawn.

method.name: get_water_material
method.description: The surface's material (the river's shader), shared by every sea cave.

method.name: get_wave_rms
method.description: The short waves' rms height over a sea cave's surface, in metres (0 without [member wavelets]).

method.name: update_now
method.description: Rebuilds the surfaces from the network now, stepping the waves [param delta] seconds. It does so every frame; this is for tests and stills.

method.name: warm_up
method.description: Steps the waves [param seconds] without drawing in between, then builds the surfaces once. For stills: the waves take about a minute to run a cave and back.

members.member: The [code]CaveNetwork3D[/code] whose sea caves are drawn.

How far in from the arch, in metres, the ocean's surface hands over to this one. Raster blends the two; the path tracer picks one surface per sample (stochastic transparency), which its samples average.
Metres between rows of vertices along the passage.
How far the surface runs past the passage's half width into the walls, in metres, so no gap shows at the rock.
The share of a wave's height kept when it reflects off a wall or the back of the cave (rough rock scatters the rest).
Seconds for the short waves to lose 1/e of their height (friction, breaking on the rock).
The rms height, in metres, of the short waves coming in at the mouth. Below 0 it follows the sea there: its rms height times [member wave_inflow_share].
The share of the sea's rms height at the mouth that comes in as short waves (the rest is the surge's long wave).
The short waves on the surface. Off, it is the surge's level alone.
The current, in m/s, where white water starts. It is full at twice this speed.
